The reproduced records in `implementation/commands.jsonl` lines 29 and 30 have exit 1 and missing-file stderr for incorrect mode and Unslop paths. Narrow the supported claim to the application tests and equivalence commands passing. Those records reproduce the errors; they are not original first-attempt captures.
3. The late audit and reconstructed TSV do not establish contemporaneous logging, complete transcript coverage or a clean full-mode execution. The original artifacts remain archived, and the current assessment explicitly separates application behavior proof from workflow conformance.

All paths under `two-seat-evidence` are relative to `/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016`; skill paths are relative to `/home/ubuntu/Dev/skills`. The archived run retains the cited source records.

digest.md.content:
# Bounded evaluation audit digest

Owner: /root. This is a late audit of retained artifacts, not the original evaluator's transcript. The TSV is reconstructed now; its timestamps record reconstruction time. No original-time logging is claimed.

The outer author merged PR #53 and ported Refactoring from the pinned pstack source. Two independently scoped fixture evaluations received the same user request and identical initial application bytes. The first used the unchanged one-seat global configuration and correctly left the main reshape incomplete; its partial subtraction passed tests, but it recorded scope, ordering and provenance failures. The second used an unmodified two-seat setup template, compared two designs, reviewed a disagreement, then produced an uncommitted map refactor and behavior pin. Its original report says all required local gates ran, but the retained read/task records omit Show me your work, its TSV and its required reviewer. The outer author identified this omission after the evaluator returned. Original reports remain unchanged.

The outer author directly read the source diff and replayed 87 CLI cases and 119 imported API cases against the original. Six tests pass. Before/subtracted/final snapshots each pass six tests and 87 CLI cases; no Git delivery commits exist. The negative-control label change is detected. Public files and saved settings are unchanged except format.cjs and the added characterization tests in the isolated fixture.

The Map result has an observed difference if Map.prototype.get is replaced. Both Interrogate reviewers demonstrated it; the lead accepted ordinary built-ins as an environment assumption. This is a bounded application result, not universal equivalence.

The second run also reports a stale installed helper read, failed initial path/bootstrap attempts, recaptured first reads and late conversion of the throughput checkpoint into host-plan items. Full chronological transcript coverage is unavailable. This audit must preserve those limits and must not certify full mode conformance retroactively.

Scope: read the log and actual cited artifacts; write only findings under parent-audit/reviewer. No source/configuration/log edits, tests, installs, publication or subdelegation. Check that the decision rows are supported, identify overclaims and missing gates, and return exact citations. The separate global-configuration case is archived in research/jstack/evaluations/refactoring/one-seat-evaluation.json; it is context, not a second application to redo.

The bounded audit is complete. The retained evidence supports a successful local application refactor under ordinary native JavaScript built-ins. It does not establish complete Juan-mode execution. This is review task `/root/refactoring_trail_audit`, using the explicit current authoring source `juancamiloqhz/skills`. I reviewed `/root`'s eight reconstructed rows at `parent-audit/decisions.tsv:2` through line 9 and its two corrective rows at lines 10 and 11. Paths below are relative to `/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/` unless absolute. The log timestamps record reconstruction time. The available history is the labeled digest and retained artifacts, not the original conversation. I did not run application commands or tests, edit the log, change source or settings, publish, install, or delegate.

The retained preflight selected the scalar `judgment and prose` role, explicit `/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-models.json`, and target `null`. The final implementation checks have stronger evidence than a success exit alone. `two-seat-evidence/commands.jsonl:41` retains six passing test results and `:42` retains zero mismatches over 368 function cases and 20 CLI invocations. The read metadata records current artifact hashes for this audit, not historical attestation. Some earlier tool outputs in this review were truncated by output limits. I followed with bounded reads of the decisive commands, report lines, JSON fields and source hashes. No failure or missing history was recast as an original success.

No jstack implementation changed during this audit. The upstream-fidelity policy was read. Comparing a changed jstack implementation with its upstream pin is therefore outside this bounded review; this report does not certify the outer Refactoring port's fidelity or the one-seat evaluation.

## Attention

reviewed by codex/gpt-6-astra, inherited selection reported by captured preflight; child runtime identity is not independently attested

- The original completion claim is too broad. `two-seat-evidence/final-report.md:19` says no required local gate remains pending, while the mode required a decision trail and the trail skill required a separate reviewer at `/home/ubuntu/Dev/skills/skills/jstack/jstack-show-me-your-work/SKILL.md:70`. The coordinator corrected the claim in log line 10 and `parent-audit/corrections.md:5`, leaving the original report unchanged. Historical full-mode conformance remains unestablished.
- Log line 9's weak evidence pointer is corrected by line 10. Its original target, `two-seat-evidence/missing-gates.md:3`, reports completed implementation gates and never names the omitted trail. The correction supplies the digest, task ledger and mode requirement. For line 7's wording about all captured slices, read line 8's separate `slice-verification.json` pointer alongside the final-output record.
- The execution-success overclaim is corrected by log line 11. `two-seat-evidence/implementation/result.md:11` says "No execution or test failed." The same paragraph acknowledges failed paths, and `implementation/commands.jsonl:29` and `:30` retain exit-1 lookup failures. `implementation/capture.json:5` identifies them as reproductions, not original command captures. The correction preserves passing application tests while retaining lookup failures. The earlier exit-127 recorder failure remains reported at `early-command-record.md:3`, without original raw output available in this audit.
- Preserve provenance gaps. `how/audit-notes.md:1` discloses a stale installed helper read and recaptured reads; `missing-gates.md:11` and `:13` disclose further recapture and late host-plan formalization. No full original transcript is available to verify every original read, timing claim or fork. Snapshot replay and a late review cannot supply that history.
- Preserve the Map assumption and reduced reviewer independence. The changed-built-in probes show a real difference, and `synthesis.md:13` deliberately accepts the narrower environment. Separate inherited contexts do not provide different-family review. Neither limit invalidates the demonstrated ordinary-built-in test results, but both limit the conclusion.
